Investor Group to Take U.K. Hospital Operator Spire Private for $1.4 Billion
By Adria Calatayud
A consortium of three investment firms agreed to take Spire Healthcare private in a deal that values the U.K. hospital operator as a whole at about 1.03 billion pounds ($1.39 billion).

The consortium formed by Spire shareholder Toscafund Asset Management, together with Three Hills and Ares, said it reached an agreement with the Spire board on the terms of a takeover offer of 250 pence a share in cash.
The price represents a 5% premium to Spire's closing share price on Friday and a 66% premium to its last price before the takeover interest became public in May.

The consortium said Spire's public-market valuation doesn't reflect the company's property and asset base, and that taking it private would unlock long-term value. Toscafund has been an investor in Spire since 2021 and supports it.
Spire said its directors intend to recommend unanimously that shareholders back the takeover.

The company separately said Justin Ash would retire as chief executive and that David Sloman, nonexecutive director and vice chair, would assume the role of interim CEO. A search to appoint a successor is under way, it added.
